title: India legal information answer rules
source: Starter guidance; use official legislation and court sources for substantive law
content: Answering rules for India-focused legal information: (1) State that responses are general legal information, not legal advice. (2) Ask which state or union territory applies when procedure or local law may vary. (3) Do not invent an Act, section, rule, deadline, fee, case, or legal outcome. (4) Prefer the current text of legislation from India Code (https://www.indiacode.nic.in/) and Gazette notifications from the Gazette of India (https://egazette.gov.in/); for court decisions, prefer the relevant official court website. (5) Name the source used and identify when the uploaded source does not establish that a rule is current. (6) Recommend a qualified Indian lawyer for fact-specific disputes, deadlines, criminal matters, or urgent action. This guide contains response safeguards, not substantive legal rules.

title: Basic Indian laws: constitutional rights, consumers, RTI, and contracts
source: Constitution of India (Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice); Consumer Protection Act, 2019; Right to Information Act, 2005; Indian Contract Act, 1872 (official texts searchable at https://www.indiacode.nic.in/)
content:
PLAIN-LANGUAGE STARTER SUMMARY, NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Check the current consolidated law, amendments, rules, and state-specific procedure before relying on any summary.

CONSTITUTION OF INDIA
- Article 14: The State must not deny any person equality before the law or equal protection of the laws in India.
- Article 19(1): Citizens have specified freedoms, including speech and expression, peaceful assembly without arms, association, movement, residence, and occupation/business. These freedoms are subject to the restrictions described in clauses (2) to (6); they are not unlimited.
- Article 21: No person may be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
- Article 21A: The State must provide free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14 in the manner provided by law.
- Article 32: A person may approach the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights in Part III; the Court has power to issue appropriate directions, orders, or writs. The correct remedy depends on the facts and applicable procedure.

CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019
- Section 2(9) describes consumer rights, including protection from hazardous goods/services, information about goods/services, access to choice, being heard, seeking redress against qualifying unfair or restrictive practices and exploitation, and consumer awareness. The Act provides consumer dispute redressal commissions; the applicable forum, procedure, limitation, and remedies depend on the claim and current rules.

RIGHT TO INFORMATION ACT, 2005
- An Indian citizen may request information from a public authority under the Act, subject to statutory exemptions and procedure. Section 7 generally requires a decision within 30 days; where the information sought concerns a person's life or liberty, the Act provides a 48-hour period. Check the Act for counting rules, transfers, fees, exemptions, and appeal procedure before advising on a particular request.

INDIAN CONTRACT ACT, 1872
- Section 10 says agreements are contracts when made with free consent by parties competent to contract, for lawful consideration and a lawful object, and when they are not expressly declared void. Whether a particular agreement meets these requirements depends on its terms and facts; other statutes may also apply.

Use these summaries only as orientation. Cite the relevant Article or section, identify the official text used, and do not infer a person's rights or likely outcome without the complete facts. Official Constitution source: https://legislative.gov.in/constitution-of-india/. Official legislation database: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/.
